chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the minimum distance at which the traveler shortens (his prayer)?' He said, 'Barid.' There is no contradiction between these two reports and the first two reports, because the meaning in them is that when the traveler intends to return on his day, shortening becomes obligatory upon him for four farsakhs. What indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.فَرَاسِخَ: farsakhs (plural of farsakh, a unit of distance)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum distance a Muslim must travel to shorten their prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential threshold for *Qasr* (shortening prayers), identifying 'Barid' as the minimum distance while linking it to the obligation arising after four farsakhs if the traveler intends an immediate return. This resolves apparent discrepancies among hadiths by distinguishing between the general definition of travel and the specific condition triggering the mandatory shortening of prayers. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent (*niyyah*) and precise measurement in determining ritual obligations.
